pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that (1 mark)
   A. shows an action
   B. describes a colour only
   C. joins two sentences
   D. names a person, animal, place or thing

2. Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs? (1 mark)
   A. To sell them
   B. To throw them away
   C. To hide them
   D. So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten

3. Reading a text once for the general meaning is done (1 mark)
   A. last, after everything
   B. first, before looking at details
   C. never
   D. only with a partner

4. A word bank is (1 mark)
   A. a class list of useful words on one theme
   B. a kind of poem
   C. a type of song
   D. a place for money

5. Which pencil grip is best? (1 mark)
   A. Grip it with a fist
   B. Hold it by the end with your teeth
   C. Press it very hard
   D. Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger

6. Which instruction is clearer? (1 mark)
   A. Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   B. Do the thing.
   C. Go and do it.
   D. Put it there.

7. Which game teaches that messages can change when passed on? (1 mark)
   A. Football
   B. Chinese whisper
   C. Hide and seek only
   D. Skipping

8. Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show? (1 mark)
   A. Boredom
   B. Sleepiness
   C. Sadness
   D. Excitement

9. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The number of words
   B. The spelling of words
   C. The size of letters
   D. The rise and fall of the voice

10. What does reading with expression mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading in whispers
   B. Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   C. Reading in a flat voice
   D. Reading without stopping

11. Which sentence needs a verb to be complete: Always ______ your hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. soap
   C. hands
   D. wash

12. Which of these is a safety rule from the road safety dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Play on the road
   B. Look right, then left, then right again
   C. Run across without looking
   D. Cross anywhere

13. What is a word puzzle used for? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking
   B. Painting
   C. Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   D. Running

14. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a conversation between two or more people
   B. a song
   C. a picture
   D. a long poem

15. Why should you not translate a saying from your language word for word? (1 mark)
   A. It is against the law
   B. It is always easy
   C. The meaning may be lost
   D. Words are never important

16. In The farmer was weary after a long day in the shamba, weary means (1 mark)
   A. very tired
   B. very hungry
   C. very loud
   D. very rich

17. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading many books widely for pleasure
   B. Copying a book
   C. Reading one word only
   D. Reading only the title

18. What does Many hands make light work mean? (1 mark)
   A. Work is always easy
   B. Nobody should help
   C. Hands are light
   D. Work is easier when people share it

19. How should a proverb be used in a composition? (1 mark)
   A. With no meaning
   B. In a way that fits the story
   C. Anywhere at all
   D. Only at the start

20. Why might a class record narrations on a device? (1 mark)
   A. To erase them
   B. To sell them
   C. To listen back and improve
   D. To waste time

21. What is the language train game? (1 mark)
   A. A running race
   B. Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   C. A reading test
   D. A game with real trains

22. Where can the main idea often be found? (1 mark)
   A. In the page number
   B. Nowhere
   C. Only in the last word
   D. In the first sentence of a paragraph

23. Which word shows a choice? (1 mark)
   A. but
   B. or
   C. so
   D. and

24. What does a simple sentence have? (1 mark)
   A. Two subjects always
   B. No capital
   C. No verb
   D. One subject and one predicate

25. Why record yourself reciting? (1 mark)
   A. To lose the poem
   B. To listen back and improve
   C. To stop practising
   D. To delete your voice

26. What is a singing game with interjections? (1 mark)
   A. A silent game
   B. A story
   C. A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   D. A written test

27. Which describes an object by size and colour? (1 mark)
   A. A bag
   B. Bagging
   C. To bag
   D. A big red bag

28. Which is a part of a form? (1 mark)
   A. Title
   B. Ending song
   C. Poem
   D. Riddle

29. What does a moderator do in a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Speaks all the time
   B. Sleeps
   C. Guides the discussion and gives turns
   D. Leaves

30. Which word helps to show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. Table
   B. Finally
   C. Yesterday
   D. Green

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)

32. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

33. Describe what a written dialogue shows. (2 marks)

34. Write three sentences describing where things are in your classroom. Use a different preposition in each. (3 marks)

35. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

36. Explain what the proverb Honesty is the best policy means. (2 marks)

37. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)

38. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

39. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

40. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

41. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

42. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)

43. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

44. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

45. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

46. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — names a person, animal, place or thing
   Nouns are naming words.

2. D — So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

3. B — first, before looking at details
   A first reading gives the main idea.

4. A — a class list of useful words on one theme
   A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

5. D — Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   A light grip prevents tiredness.

6. A — Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   It says what, where and why.

7. B — Chinese whisper
   In Chinese whisper the message changes as it passes.

8. D — Excitement
   Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

9. D — The rise and fall of the voice
   Intonation is voice movement.

10. B — Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   Expression shows the feelings in the text.

11. D — wash
   Wash is the action word that completes the sentence.

12. B — Look right, then left, then right again
   The dialogue teaches how to look before crossing.

13. C — Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   Puzzles help pupils remember words.

14. A — a conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue records people speaking to each other.

15. C — The meaning may be lost
   Sayings often carry meaning beyond the words.

16. A — very tired
   A long day of work suggests tiredness.

17. A — Reading many books widely for pleasure
   Extensive reading means reading a lot for enjoyment.

18. D — Work is easier when people share it
   It is a proverb about working together.

19. B — In a way that fits the story
   A proverb should match the lesson of the story.

20. C — To listen back and improve
   Recordings show what to improve.

21. B — Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   Each pupil adds a when sentence.

22. D — In the first sentence of a paragraph
   First sentences often give the main idea.

23. B — or
   Or offers a choice.

24. D — One subject and one predicate
   Simple sentences have one main idea.

25. B — To listen back and improve
   Playback shows how to improve.

26. C — A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   Interjections can be part of songs.

27. D — A big red bag
   Big and red are adjectives.

28. A — Title
   A form has a title.

29. C — Guides the discussion and gives turns
   The moderator keeps order.

30. B — Finally
   Finally shows the last step.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people written to show what each speaker says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for showing speakers' words.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example The board is in front of the class. My bag is under my desk. The teacher stands beside the door.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Telling the truth is always the wisest choice because it builds trust.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the reason.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
